title: Unfathomed - Cosmic Horror Music Pack, Dark Orchestral and Choir BGM - 44 Tracks
tagline: 44 track cosmic horror score in five acts that descend from lydian to phrygian, a wordless choir in every track.
description:
Unfathomed is a 44 track cosmic horror music pack for investigation, exploration and survival horror games: 38 full looping pieces and 6 short cues, 59:38 of music, as OGG files with sample accurate loop tags plus all 44 editable MIDI sources. RPG Maker MV and MZ read the loop points with no plugin, and the Readme gives the import steps for Godot 4 (followed in a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files), Unity and GameMaker. Royalty free for commercial games. Three full tracks are free to download on this page, with their MIDI.

One investigation, from the observatory down to the abyss, in five acts. Act 1, The Surface (lydian): "Unfathomed", "The Observatory", "Letters from the Coast", "The Harbour Town", "A Strange Light at Sea" and "The Lighthouse Keeper". Act 2, The Shallows (ionian, then mixolydian): "The Expedition Sets Out", "The Society Library", "The Fishing Village", "Down to the Boats", "Sounding the Depths", "The Professor's Study", "Rumours at the Inn" and "The Old Church". Act 3, The Twilight (dorian): "The Cult", "Carvings in the Rock", "The Night Procession", "Fog on the Water", "The Diving Bell", "Something Follows" and "Ritual on the Shore". Act 4, The Midnight (aeolian): "The Descent", "The Drowned City", "The Impossible Halls", "The Sighting", "Pursuit in the Dark", "The Madness", "The Cultists' Hymn" and "The Spawn". Act 5, The Abyss (phrygian): "The Abyss", "The Gate Beneath", "The Sleeper Stirs", "It Wakes", "The Unravelling", "The Stars Are Right", "What Lies Beyond", "The Survivor's Account" and "Unfathomed (Credits)". Cues: "A Glimpse", "Sanity Slips", "An Artefact", "The Door Opens", "Consumed" and "Survived".

The descent. The record goes down and never climbs back: across all 44 tracks in order, no track is in a brighter mode than the one before it. It opens in lydian, the brightest of the six modes on this record, and ends in phrygian, the darkest of them; each mode in the order differs from the one before it by exactly one degree, so the light goes out of the harmony one degree at a time as the investigation goes deeper. Every note on the record is in its track's mode (20,973 notes read in the shipped MIDI, 0 outside), all seven tones of the mode sound in every track, and every track sounds its own mode's colour note, the one that tells it from a mode next to it in the order: lydian's raised fourth, ionian's major seventh, mixolydian's flat seventh, dorian's major sixth, aeolian's minor sixth and phrygian's flat second (2,450 colour notes in all). Read against the five other modes on its own tonic, every track fails all five (220 of 220 readings), so the mode on each track is the only one its notes fit.

One theme, one choir. The seed theme, The Fathom Line, falls three steps and reaches back up a third, and all 44 tracks state it in its own shape, counted by the harness in the finished MIDI. Four more themes come with it: The Deep is the seed turned over, for the sighting, the pursuit and the spawn; The Star climbs a fourth in even quarters, for the observatory, the strange light at sea and the expedition; The Rite turns on four quick eighths, for the cult, the night procession and the hymn; The Tide opens on a held half note, for the harbour town, the fog and the drowned city. A wordless choir sings in all 44 tracks, 10,351 notes: it holds the chords in 38 of them and carries the tune in 6. 2,113 statements and fragments of the 5 themes across the album.

Loops of a minute. Investigation and exploration games stay on one screen for a long time, so all 38 full pieces loop for at least a minute before they repeat: the shortest loop is 64.8 seconds, read from the LOOPLENGTH tag of the shipped OGG files. 5 of the faster pieces carry a third section to stay over the minute.

What is in it. 38 full pieces and 6 cues, 59:38 of music, 41 keys, 60 to 120 BPM, all in 4/4. 30 General MIDI instruments: piano, celesta, music box, vibraphone, tubular bells, reed organ, acoustic bass, violin, viola, cello, contrabass, tremolo strings, harp, timpani, strings, slow strings, choir, voice oohs, trombone, tuba, muted trumpet, French horn, brass section, oboe, English horn, bassoon, clarinet, flute, shakuhachi and whistle. There is no drum kit and no synth; the only percussion is tuned: celesta (220 notes), music box (144 notes), vibraphone (148 notes), tubular bells (104 notes) and timpani (572 notes). It is a score, not a sound design pack: every sound is a written note, with no noise beds and no tape effects.

What you get. 44 OGG files, 38 of them with sample accurate LOOPSTART and LOOPLENGTH tags, which is what RPG Maker MV and MZ read; each looping file ends exactly at its loop end. 44 editable .mid sources. A Readme with per engine import notes, the proof reports, and a royalty free commercial licence.

Gate results. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, and the reports ship inside the download. They say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks are for.

Three full tracks are free on this page, with their MIDI: "The Observatory" from the top of the descent (lydian), "The Sighting" from Act 4 (aeolian) and "The Abyss" from the bottom (phrygian).

An honest note. The renders are a General MIDI reference render through a conventional soundfont, and the instruments are the General MIDI sounds of those names; the MIDI is there so you can use your own. No game, book or film cue is quoted; every tune was composed for this record. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used anywhere.

devlog.title: Unfathomed is out: a 44 track cosmic horror score that descends through six modes
devlog.body:
Unfathomed is a 44 track music pack for investigation, exploration and survival horror games: one investigation from the observatory and the harbour town down through the cult, the diving bell, the drowned city and the abyss, plus six short cues. It is live now, with three full tracks free to download from the page.

The idea. The record descends. It is in five acts, and across all 44 tracks in order no track is in a brighter mode than the one before it: lydian at the top, then ionian, mixolydian, dorian and aeolian, down to phrygian at the bottom. Every note is in its track's mode (20,973 notes read in the shipped MIDI, 0 outside) and every track sounds its own mode's colour note. A wordless choir sings in all 44 tracks, all 38 full pieces loop for a minute or more (shortest 64.8 seconds), and the seed theme is stated in its own shape in all 44.

How it was checked. 788 theory checks and 510 audio checks, 0 failed, with the reports inside the download. The loop tags were followed into a blank Godot 4.7.2 project, all 44 files. Those numbers say the music is correctly written, rendered and tagged. They are not a claim about taste, which is what the free tracks ("The Observatory", "The Sighting" and "The Abyss") are for.

The renders are a General MIDI reference render; the MIDI is there so you can move it to your own sounds. No game, book or film cue is quoted. The composition system is AI written code and no generative audio model is used.
